mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising real discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters as of snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.5% for three consecutive months as of snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of persistent sub-5.5% unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average at snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where both GDPC1 and HOUST jointly signal weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months as of snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg AND FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg at snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both inflation and rates exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) following a >1% monthly payroll gain.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months, coupled with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals deteriorating consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 is flat or falling at snapshot
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when both RSAFS and GDPC1 jointly signal demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during sustained above-average HOUST readings.
